positions.name: Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical Inc.
positions.catalyst: The FDA granted FULL approval of FAYUVI (rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf, formerly UX111) at ~3:57pm ET Thursday — roughly three minutes before the closing bell. It is the first-ever approved treatment for Sanfilippo syndrome Type A (MPS IIIA), a fatal pediatric lysosomal storage disease with a median life expectancy of 15 years, and it is Ultragenyx's second approved gene therapy. The approval rests on the pivotal Transpher A trial with follow-up now extending nearly eight years: treated patients (mITT, N=17) scored 23.5 points higher on the Bayley-III cognitive scale than an untreated external natural-history cohort (N=27), p<0.0001. Critically, the approval carries a Priority Review Voucher — PRVs have historically sold to other drugmakers for hundreds of millions of dollars, against a total market cap of only $1.43B. Commercial product is expected to reach Qualified Treatment Centers within 30 to 60 days.
positions.driver: This is the cleanest asymmetry on the board because the catastrophic binary already happened and is already priced. On Sept 3 the Phase 3 Aspire study of apazunersen in Angelman syndrome missed both its primary and a key secondary endpoint; RARE fell 44% in a session on 19.8M shares and analysts cut price targets to roughly $16.53 (Baird, Evercore ISI). The stock then bled to a 52-week low of $12.73 on Sept 16 — two days ago. What is left after that washout is a company with two approved gene therapies, four marketed products (Crysvita, Mepsevii, Dojolvi, Evkeeza), and a sellable voucher, at a $1.43B cap. The approval landed with three minutes left in Thursday's session, so the market had essentially no opportunity to price it: RARE closed at $14.50, up 12.58%, AT the session high ($14.57) on 12.4M shares versus a 5.3M 30-day average — a capitulation low followed immediately by a catalyst reversal on 2.3x volume. Entry at $14.74 is only +1.66% over the prior close, far inside the do-not-chase band, versus the semiconductor complex where today's alternatives (INTC +2.9% after +9.7% Thursday, GLW +3.2%) are day three of a beta rebound with no fresh company news. Liquid enough many times over for this book: ~5.3M-8.5M shares/day, $77-123M notional. RSI 28, trading at ~6.5% of its 52-week range, down 50% over twelve months — positioning is empty and the takeover chatter (BioMarin floated publicly after the Angelman failure) is a live free option.
positions.risks: MPS IIIA is ultra-rare — incidence near 1 in 70,000 births — so the approved product's own revenue ramp will be small and slow regardless of pricing; a meaningful part of this thesis rests on the Priority Review Voucher, whose sale is neither guaranteed nor time-certain. Sell-the-news is the direct risk: the stock already gained 12.58% Thursday, and gene-therapy approvals in ultra-rare indications have repeatedly been faded. The FAYUVI label carries warnings for blood-clotting complications and tumor formation and requires immunosuppressive steroids around dosing, which is a real commercial headwind at launch. The company is cutting costs after the Angelman failure and runs negative earnings (P/E -2.48, P/B -4.90), so financing risk is live and an equity raise into strength would be punishing. STOP CAVEAT — the $13.71 stop is 7% below entry, the maximum this book allows, but Thursday's intraday low was $13.20 and the Sept 16 52-week low was $12.73, both BELOW the stop; a full retrace of the approval pop stops this out before reaching prior support. That is an accepted, explicit trade-off, not an oversight. Position is also held across a weekend (rotation is Monday) into an active Middle East conflict, and today is September quad-witching with the S&P quarterly rebalance effective at the close, so index-mechanical volume will be abnormal.
